newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary GDP growth slowly picking up - OECD.
newsitem.headline: Hungary GDP growth slowly picking up - OECD.

text.p: Hungary's GDP growth is slowly picking up, fueled mainly by exports, while domestic demand is stabilising after a shock austerity programme, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said.

"The devaluation of the forint and real wage declines improved international competitiveness and will contribute to strong export performance," the OECD said in its December 1996 Economic Outlook Hungary.
It predicted that growth in gross domestic product, which slowed to 1.5 percent in 1995 and is estimated at 0.5 percent this year, would recover to 1.7 percent next year and 3.2 percent in 1998.
It said investment growth would play a major role, with gross fixed capital formation doubling to 8.0 percent in 1997 from 4.0 percent this year, and rising to 9.0 percent in 1998.

Consumer spending should also recover after taking a nosedive with the introduction in March 1995 of an austerity programme that included an eight percent import surcharge and introduced a 1.3 percent monthly crawling peg devaluation of the forint, since reduced to 1.2 percent.
The austerity plan has caused a sharp drop in real wages and real disposable income while unemployment has stuck persistently above 10 percent, but the report said this should change.

"Household incomes and consumption should stabilise in 1997 before resuming growth in 1998," the OECD said. "While restructuring will translate into continued employment losses and labour force contraction, by 1998 the labour market should have stopped shrinking."
The report said inflation in Hungary was declining but would remain well above the OECD average for the time being.

"Twelve-month consumer price inflation has fallen to 21 percent from 30 percent in June 1995," the OECD said. "Although consumer confidence is very low, it has been improving and business expectations are positive on balance."
